thread.title: Qualcomm: Potential 7% Dividend Yield - Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM)

author: Big Alpha Research
title: Qualcomm: Potential 7% Dividend Yield - Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ:QCOM)
text:
Background In July 2018, Qualcomm ( QCOM ) announced a tender notice to buy back $10 billion worth of shares at a price between $60 and $67.50. As part of a broader buyback program, QCOM expects to buy $30 billion worth of shares by fiscal year 2019. The offer ended on August 27 and share price subsequently ran up to a high of $76.50 in September before a subsequent decline in shares. QCOM currently trades at $55.
Why I am keen to invest in QCOM The overarching theme for my investment portfolio is to invest and grow my current savings in 7 years to hit my retirement goal of $2m after which my family hopes to pursue our interests and hobbies or find meaningful work to do. The intention is that a 4% or 5% annual return from the portfolio should cover our lifestyle expenses.
More about my initial thoughts on planning for my portfolio and retirement ideas were written in this article on Seeking Alpha. QCOM had been shortlisted since October because the portfolio requires a high growth potential and at valuations that are undemanding. Broadly, I have been looking at stocks that trade below 15x P/E and exhibits EPS growth and/or demonstrates a potential growth driver that caters to future demand. Some other ideas generated include Gentex ( GNTX ) and Magna International ( MGA ) but the screen also threw up ideas like Tatneft .
QCOM has a superb record in owning intellectual property and a number of mobile phone brands including Apple ( AAPL ) uses QCOM's technology. To the extent Apple is disputing QCOM's legal right to charge the company royalties. Although this long drawn dispute is a drag on stocks and probably will continue well into 2019, the investment theme is a firm bet on the large scale deployment of 5G technology.
5th Generation Mobile Network or 5G, will elevate the mobile network to interconnect people and allow people to control or interconnect machines with machines. 5G will deliver multi-Gbps peak rates, ultra-low latency, massive capacity, and more uniform user experience. What it means is that a world fully deployed in 5G will allow smart cities to be built, IoT to proliferate . Machina Research forecasts “IoT will account for one-quarter of the global 41 million 5G connections in 2024.”
IoT is also a feature in my portfolio's investment theme especially enablers and participants in the future auto industry. Imagine in a world where commuters used to spend 2 hours a day getting to work and back home, the future car would act as a second screen possibly replacing your TV or phone or replicate your living room setting, where you read, communicate with friends or family, catch up on emails, control your smart home devices, or simply catch a nap before starting an intense 9 AM meeting.
QCOM is a key player in 5G. This article on Engadget aptly puts QCOM in the forefront of the world of 5G. The Snapdragon X50 5G modem features in each these mobile phone companies' flagship 5G models slated for launch in 2019.
Notable brands not on this list include Huawei, Apple and Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ). Samsung has developed its own Exynos Modem 5100 . Huawei will launch its 5G foldable screen phone in the middle of 2019, running on its modem Balong 5000.
For the same reasons why Broadcom wanted to acquire the company, why Trump wanted the deal blocked , I believe QCOM has the ability to be the leader in 5G. QCOM tops the list of patent holders which give it the same standard setting leadership position QCOM had in the 3G and 4G world.
QCOM has also aggressively marketed its superior 5G capabilities and the company had released better performance over rivals Intel in part of its courtship with mobile phone manufacturers.
Bear in mind this is a stock that was until early this year, valued as a strategic target at $117 billion. There must be something in their IP that the market is overlooking. QCOM is now trading at a market cap of $67 billion which is about 40% below the selling price.
Financials and valuation
The historical 5-year profit and loss trend looks dismal. Revenue and operating income fell 14% and 90% respectively in the past 5 years. The stock price might have experienced the same steep declines if not for QCOM's increasing dividends from $1.54 to $2.38.
Source: Marketwatch.com
From a PB perspective, QCOM has $928 million in Net Assets which means the PB multiple is 72x. The financial engineering continues as I circle back to the completion of the $10 billion share buyback and possibly another $22.9 billion to go. With $12 billion in cash and debt of $16.4 billion, QCOM may have to borrow to keep up with dividends and share purchases. This is a risky prospect especially with rising interest rates. In 2017, QCOM issued $11 billion in floating and fixed rate debt maturing between 2019 and 2047 with interest rates varying from 2.7% to 4.47%.
Source: QCOM Annual Report 2018
Over the past 3 years, a total of $37.5 billion had been used for share purchases and dividends. However, it had only issued an additional $11 billion of debt over the same period. QCOM had in fact been paring down its available-for-sale securities on the balance sheet and realizing the cash. Part of this sell-down in assets was meant to fund the NXP transaction as disclosed in QCOM's annual report section F-47.
Going forward, QCOM would likely generate adequate free cash flows to cover interest expense of $768 million (based on 2018 figure) and if an additional $11 billion of debt is taken for the share repurchase, roughly $1.5 billion in interest expense would be factored into 2019 cash flows. This would leave cash available for dividends to be roughly the same or slightly lower than 2018.
After all that financial engineering, I reckon by September 2019, QCOM would have a market cap reduced by about 1/3, at $45 billion and a possible ability to maintain dividends of $3.2 to $3.4 billion or greater, representing a decent 7% dividend yield.
Risks
Source: QCOM Q4 Selected Financial Data as of September 2018
The impact of fines in 2018 was hefty. $1.2 billion was imposed by the European Commission, a $5.7 billion tax charge. 2017 fines amounted to $1.7 billion and there was a BlackBerry (NYSE: BB ) arbitration expense of $940 million. Further fines will likely impact QCOM in 2019 and that is unavoidable given the competition for 5G dominance and rise of China's own 5G capabilities .
Conclusion With average analyst targets at $70.50 and management guiding EPS of $5.25, which is 10.5x P/E on current prices, QCOM looks like a reasonable bet with a potential to increase dividend yield and share price could be supported by further share repurchases.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
